title: ZoomIt: Jittery zoom in with Ctrl + 1

judgment.rationale: The input is sufficient for a scoped maintainer performance reproduction. A monotonic interpolation function alone cannot prove a smooth rendered transition, and 'jittery' does not identify a faulty easing curve. Measure timer/render pacing and cursor-centered geometry before choosing an animation change; do not ask for the already-supplied install/elevation metadata.
evidence: The author supplies Ctrl+1 as the trigger, 0.102.2933, Windows 11 Pro, an elevated system install, and a diagnostic ZIP.
The existing ZoomIt logs show startup/enabling but no frame timings; the archive's monitor report identifies the active display but does not measure rendered frame intervals.
Merged #50444 introduced smooth zoom animation; it is relevant change history, not an already-verified fix for this later jitter report.

Source inspected at main 9227a8497750: src/modules/ZoomIt/ZoomIt/ZoomAnimation.cpp: Sample uses elapsed time with logarithmic Hermite interpolation and Retarget preserves bounded directional velocity. https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/9227a8497750c257a0682b53c556d07f48ed8ff3/src/modules/ZoomIt/ZoomIt/ZoomAnimation.cpp

Source inspected at main 9227a8497750: src/modules/ZoomIt/ZoomIt/Zoomit.cpp: Zoom transitions sample on elapsed time and schedule Windows timer-driven animation frames; actual scheduling/render latency is separate from the interpolation calculation. https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/9227a8497750c257a0682b53c556d07f48ed8ff3/src/modules/ZoomIt/ZoomIt/Zoomit.cpp

Downloaded the existing ZIP and inspected ZoomIt module/application logs and monitor inventory. Read #50444's scope/file list; no issue-specific covering PR was found. No frame benchmark or UI run was executed here.

reproduce.title: Measure Ctrl+1 frame pacing before changing animation curves
reproduce.version_requirement: 0.102.2933 versus current stable/main; compare the author's prior release only if its version is known.
prerequisites: Use an isolated test account or controlled test machine; preserve existing user data.
steps: 1. Use the supplied elevated/system-install context; keep display scale, refresh mode and initial zoom target constant.
2. Record repeated Ctrl+1 transitions with the pointer stationary, then with controlled pointer motion and a busy-desktop control.
3. Measure timer sample times, render durations and frame-to-frame zoom/viewport position; distinguish missed frames from a non-monotonic scale or center jump.
4. Repeat zoom-out and rapid reversal/retarget without changing unrelated recording or live-zoom settings.
reproduce.expected_result: Transitions render at a stable cadence with monotonic scale and stable intended center; rapid reversal does not jump or preserve obsolete animation state.
